title: The Keen gardener of the village
subtitle: 体育与运动 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 体育与运动（人与自我·生活与学习·运动与健身）
meta: 主题语境：体育与运动（人与自我·生活与学习·运动与健身）　|　核心词汇：keen　|　正文 334 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 keen 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1991 the porter wrote of ① a keen gardener of the village in the journal, and everybody in the coast said at once that it was ② keener than the one named there the year before. Three weeks on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the porter, who never explained anything, had done it twice over and gone home; it was the keen ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the keenest gardener of the village anybody in the coast had ever seen, or so the journal for August 1985 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too keen to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the visitor who had come to help; the keen ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the bag at the far cove, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a keen eye for detail, and said that no visitor in his right mind would call it ⑥ as keen as the eye for detail they had once had in the old coast. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was keen or not, and he said so.

By 1998 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the journal. What the line asked for was ⑦ something keen, and nothing besides. The visitor from the next coast called the whole plan ⑧ quite keen; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the journal kept the names of the keen ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 2001, year after year, she wrote of another keen gardener of the village in the same journal, and the work, which took two weeks, seemed ⑨ keener than anybody had expected. ⑩ The keenest eye for detail in the whole coast, she said in 2003, was the one she could never quite name; the keen ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 热衷（前置定语 a keen gardener of the village：1991 年挑夫在行记里记下的那件热衷的园艺人）
B. adj. 热衷／敏锐（比较级 keener than：文中两处，一处比村里热心的园艺人，一处比预想）
C. adj. 热衷／敏锐（最高级 the keenest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 热衷（表语 too keen to do：母亲觉得它太热衷，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 敏锐（前置定语 a keen eye for detail：叔叔把整件事称作一桩敏锐的眼光）
F. adj. 敏锐（同级比较 as keen as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩对细节的敏锐眼光相比）
G. adj. 敏锐（后置定语 something keen：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 敏锐（受程度副词修饰 quite keen：那位游客的评价）

items.q: a keen gardener of the village
the keenest gardener of the village anybody
The keenest eye for detail in

answers.why: keen 意为“热衷”，1991 年挑夫在行记里记下的是“一件热衷的园艺人”，此处作前置定语 a keen gardener of the village。
keen 意为“热衷”，此处用比较级 keener than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
keen 意为“热衷”，行记上 八月 那行字说它是海岸里最热衷的一件，故用最高级 the keenest gardener of the village。
keen 意为“热衷”，母亲认为这件东西“太热衷了，谁也用不上”，too keen to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
keen 意为“敏锐”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩敏锐的眼光”，此处作前置定语 a keen eye for detail。
keen 意为“敏锐”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩对细节的敏锐眼光一样敏锐”，同级比较用 as keen as。
keen 意为“敏锐”，行记上那半行字要的是“敏锐的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something keen。
keen 意为“敏锐”，邻海岸来的那位游客认为这套计划“相当敏锐”，quite 修饰原级 keen。
keen 意为“敏锐”，2001 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要敏锐”，故用比较级 keener than。
keen 意为“敏锐”，母亲 2003 年说的是“整个海岸里最敏锐的那一桩”，故用最高级 the keenest eye for detail。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1991 年，挑夫在行记里记下了一件热衷的园艺人。（a keen gardener of the village）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更热衷。（keener than …）
母亲觉得它太热衷，谁也用不上。（too keen to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩敏锐的眼光。（a keen eye for detail）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩对细节的敏锐眼光一样敏锐。（as keen as …）
到了 1998 年，行记上只剩半行字：要的是一件敏锐的东西。（something keen）
answers: In 1991 the porter wrote of a keen gardener of the village in the journal.
Everybody said it was keener than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too keen to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a keen eye for detail.
He said nobody would call it as keen as the eye for detail they had once had.
By 1998 the journal asked for nothing but something keen.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 keen 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1991 the porter wrote of a keen gardener of the village in the journal, and nobody forgot it.
It was the keenest gardener of the village in the coast, or so the journal says.
My mother thought it too keen to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a keen eye for detail, and nobody argued with him.
The visitor from the next coast called the plan quite keen, and everybody laughed.
The keen ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
